note: Statuses are pilot gates ('worth testing at larger n'), NOT truth claims. No 'supported' terminal exists.

hypotheses.claim: behavior actions chain into recurring intra-message transitions (a grammar exists at all)
hypotheses.note: Eligible = records with >=2 actions. Sparse eligibility itself is the H11 caveat.

hypotheses.claim: reveal is frequently followed by self-devaluation within the same message
hypotheses.note: Eligible = records where a reveal has a following action.

hypotheses.claim: a reveal is usually masked/retracted right after it (defensive concealment)
hypotheses.note: Counterexamples = reveal-without-mask records, reported explicitly to block an overclaim.

hypotheses.claim: fear-of-abandonment couples to reassurance-seeking strategies (driver→strategy grammar)
hypotheses.note: Eligible = records with A-grade fear_of_abandonment; tierA+tierB reassurance couplings counted.

hypotheses.claim: a low observed trigger co-occurs with high inferred activation (hair-trigger sensitivity)
hypotheses.note: Eligible = low/minimal observed trigger; observed = those also high inferred activation.

hypotheses.claim: single-valence affect dominates; mixed simultaneous affect is rare
hypotheses.note: Eligible = records with a known coexistence type; 'unknown' excluded (not evidence of rarity).

hypotheses.claim: test_bond is the most frequent relationship operation
hypotheses.note: Top operation observed = test_bond. H7 asks whether test_bond leads.

hypotheses.claim: utterances are designed to elicit a specific partner operation (expected-reply grammar)
hypotheses.note: Eligible = all records; observed = records with a confident immediate expected-reply class.

hypotheses.claim: multi-beat messages carry an escalation arc more often than not
hypotheses.note: Eligible = multi-beat (>=2 action) records; observed = those with an escalation step.
Eligible = records where perform_confidence has a following action.

hypotheses.claim: most records are single-action, so cross-action grammar is sparse at this n (a limitation, stated as a hypothesis to test)
hypotheses.note: Sparsity is a finding: if most records are single-action, transition grammar needs more data.
